old: The recorded native engine experiment reports 408 Minimax/Alpha-Beta comparisons with matching values and 820 successful restoration checks. Separate adapter and browser records exercise the connection between search and the application. In the reference experiments, move ordering reduced visited nodes on some positions, but its additional evaluation work could outweigh the saving in elapsed time. A hard candidate cap discarded immediate wins in one fixture, and cache reuse after a root-player change produced an incorrect score in another. These results show that search depth and node count alone are insufficient to assess correctness or efficiency [19], [22], [27], [31], [32], [49].

The final local application provides all six report profiles: Easy, Normal, Hard, Very Hard, Expert and Master. A fresh build from the included Rust source reproduced the existing application binary byte-for-byte. Browser smoke checks selected each profile and observed a response with completed depths 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 on the checked opening. The presentation now embeds this local application. These checks establish the tested configuration and interaction; playing-strength calibration remains future work.

new:
The original reference runner requires caro-core-reference at the repository root. The current-engine research runner expects gomoku-main/engine and an application directory named 10_caro; its WASM stage copies generated files into that application. These paths belong to the original experiment workspace. The local application release instead owns its Rust source at CaroGame/engine and uses the following commands from CaroGame to rebuild it. Rust with the wasm32-unknown-unknown target and wasm-pack must be installed; the offline build also requires the locked Cargo dependencies in the local cache.
npm run build:wasm
cargo test --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml --locked --offline
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
The build writes src/game/wasm/engine/provenance.json with the input hashes, output hashes and tool versions. The 13 November build used rustc/cargo 1.98.1 and wasm-pack 0.15.0. The current engine toolchain selects stable, so a later build must record the resolved version and compare its generated hashes rather than assume identical bytes.
For the local defense demonstration, start the game with npm run dev from CaroGame, then start npm run dev from present in another terminal. The game uses port 8443 and the presentation uses port 5174. Local presentation entry points use the game on the same host at port 8443; VITE_CARO_GAME_URL can explicitly select another application endpoint. Open http://localhost:5174 for the presentation or http://localhost:8443 for the game.
The local release contains all six difficulty selectors and uses the rebuilt Worker/WASM route. The external 10-caro.vercel.app deployment was not updated in this local release and should not be used to demonstrate its six-tier contract. Regenerating the separate native reference datasets still requires their exact dependency sources and original harness layout [11], [13].

13 November local release verification. Eleven Rust source, manifest, test and example files were copied unchanged into CaroGame/engine. A locked offline wasm-pack release build, with wasm-opt disabled, regenerated the five runtime files. All five matched the previous canonical package. The WASM file is 111,582 bytes with SHA-256 1ff854e6493b39727d07cfcf69b0af06e349a748249d85d688741a4f85017989. The source and output manifest contains 16 checked hashes.
Native tests passed 38 unit and 7 integration cases. The frontend passed 65 tests in 9 files, typecheck and the Vite build. The runtime and contract subset contains 28 tests, including six paired immediate-win/forced-block cases on the actual WASM package; Easy is checked for legal Random behavior, while the other five profiles take the unique tactical completion. Browser smoke checks selected each tier and observed completed depths 0/1/2/3/4/5 after the checked opening move. This is finite configuration and interaction evidence, without a tournament-strength conclusion.
The presentation was built after its playable entry points were switched to the local application. The previous public deployment served four selectors and a different 48,549-byte WASM package; the local release does not replace that deployment. The rebuild and application checks retain their own evidence files: ENGINE_MIGRATION_SOURCE_PARITY.json, WASM_REBUILD_RUNTIME_EVIDENCE.json, ENGINE_MIGRATION_VERIFICATION.md and src/game/wasm/engine/provenance.json.
